set_aside.subject: alias disclosure classification
set_aside.text: “an alias whose content breaks the rule does reach the agent” and “the alias is held as `business_confidential`, not `personal_data`” contradict R0-26’s “A `personal_data` value leaves Registry to the owner and to a service whose token allows that class — never to an agent” when the alias contains a person’s name, address or other identifying content
set_aside.question: Is disclosure determined permanently by the alias field’s declared class, even when its actual value is personal data, or must Registry prevent such a value from reaching the agent to preserve R0-26’s value-level guarantee?
options: Always treat the alias field as `business_confidential` and return its value to the agent
Treat an identifying alias value as `personal_data` and withhold or refuse it
Narrow R0-26 explicitly so its guarantee applies only to fields classified as `personal_data`, not to misclassified content
set_aside.default_guess: Treat the field as `business_confidential` and return it, while narrowing R0-26’s guarantee to Registry’s declared field classifications.

witness.initial: A project’s alias is the customer’s full name, is no longer than 40 characters, and the project is granted to an agent session.
events: The agent requests the project projection through Cabinet Kernel.
outcomes: Registry returns the alias because the alias field is `business_confidential`.
Registry withholds or refuses the alias because its value is personal data and R0-26 says no personal-data value reaches an agent.
witness.observer: The agent sees the customer’s name in one implementation and not in the other.

set_aside.subject: alias length model
set_aside.question: What exactly counts as a character, and is the value normalized before its length is measured?
options: Count Unicode code points without normalization
Normalize to a specified Unicode form and then count code points
Measure encoded bytes or implementation-language code units
set_aside.default_guess: Normalize to Unicode NFC and count Unicode code points.

witness.initial: The owner supplies an alias whose displayed text is 40 grapheme clusters but whose decomposed representation contains more than 40 Unicode code points.
events: The owner submits the alias on an operation that sets it.
outcomes: Registry accepts it because it contains 40 displayed characters.
Registry refuses it because its stored representation contains more than 40 code points or code units.
witness.observer: The owner sees acceptance in one implementation and refusal in the other.

set_aside.subject: operations that set an alias
set_aside.question: On which concrete operations may an alias be supplied, changed, cleared or removed, and therefore where must the 40-character check run?
options: Create, project correction and migration import may set it; correction may also clear it
Only project creation and migration import may set it
Any owner project-card correction may add, replace or clear it
Alias has a separate owner action
set_aside.default_guess: Allow it on project creation, project correction and migration import; allow correction to clear it; apply the same validation to every non-absent value.

witness.initial: An active project exists without an alias.
events: The owner opens the project card and attempts to add a 20-character alias.
A careful implementation interprets the available owner actions.
outcomes: The correction is accepted because correcting the project card may set the alias.
The correction is unavailable or refused because the texts never assign alias changes to project correction.
witness.observer: The owner sees either an editable alias or no way to add one after creation.
